issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) require the Animal constructor and the getName/setName methods to have protected visibility, but the provided solution defines a public constructor and public getter/setter. This visibility mismatch contradicts the specification and UML and may confuse students about the intended access level for these members.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal constructor and the getName/setName methods protected to match the UML and problem statement (change the constructor and accessor methods from public to protected). Update any dependent code accordingly (subclasses can still access them).

issues.description: The template Farm.java defines singFarmSongVerse without an Animal parameter (the parameter is commented out), while the problem specification and the solution implement singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). The missing parameter in the template method signature is a structural mismatch that will force students to modify the method signature rather than only implementing the method body.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the Animal parameter in the template method signature: change singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) to singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) so the template matches the specification and students can implement the verse printing without having to alter the method signature.
